questions.stem: Which embryonic structure gives rise to the vertebrae?

Which muscles are primarily responsible for shoulder extension and elbow extension?

choices.E: Flexor digitorum superficialis and Triceps brachii

questions.stem: A man falls asleep with his arm draped over the back of a chair after a party. The next morning, he is unable to extend his wrist and fingers. Which nerve is most likely injured?
A middle-aged man presents with wrist drop following a fracture of the humerus. Which part of the humerus is most likely fractured?
A patient presents with wrist drop. Which nerve is most likely injured?
Which muscle originates from the subscapular fossa of the scapula?
Which spinal nerve roots contribute to the innervation of structures extending inferiorly toward the iliac crest?

A 53-year-old man presents with pain on the left side of his neck radiating down his arm to the middle finger. On examination, he has weakness of the triceps brachii, decreased sensation over the dorsum of the hand and middle finger, and a unilateral decrease in the triceps reflex. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old backpacker presents with a history of low back pain and, more recently, right leg pain. On examination, he has gastrocnemius muscle atrophy, weak ankle plantar flexion, decreased sensation over the lateral aspect of the foot, and a diminished Achilles tendon reflex. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Where is the insertion point of the latissimus dorsi muscle located?
Which location should be palpated to assess the dorsalis pedis pulse?

choices.D: Medial to the flexor hallucis longus tendon

questions.stem: Which muscle is primarily responsible for flexion of the thigh at the hip joint?
Hypertrophy of which ligament commonly causes vertebral (spinal) canal stenosis?
A positive Trendelenburg test indicates weakness of which of the following muscles?
Which artery is the most susceptible to injury in a femoral neck fracture?

A 45-year-old woman presents with medial knee pain that worsens when climbing stairs. Physical examination reveals pain and tenderness at the inferomedial aspect of the patella and tenderness over the medial tibial condyle. Which of the following structures is the most likely cause of the medial knee pain?
Which of the following tests is used to assess hamstring muscle strength?

choices.A: Resisted knee flexion while in the prone position
choices.C: Resisted hip abduction in the side-lying position
choices.D: Resisted hip flexion in the sitting position

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man presents with posterior calf pain after jogging. The pain worsens with plantar flexion of the ankle when the knee is extended but improves slightly when the knee is flexed. Which muscle is most likely injured?
A patient presents with a mass compressing a peripheral nerve and is unable to dorsiflex the ankle. Which nerve is most likely affected?

A 25-year-old athlete presents lateral foot pain after twisting his foot during a soccer match. X-ray reveals an avulsion fracture at the base of the 5th metatarsal. Which of the following muscles is most likely involved in this injury?

A 45-year-old office worker presents with numbness and tingling in his right hand. He reports difficulty feeling objects when touching them with his thumb, index finger, and middle finger. Physical examination reveals decreased sensation over the palmar aspect of the index finger and lateral half of the ring finger. Which nerve is most likely injured?

A 45-year-old man presents with numbness, tingling, and burning pain over the anterolateral aspect of his thigh. He has no muscle weakness or loss of reflexes. The symptoms worsen when standing or walking for a long period. Which nerve is most likely affected?

A 50-year-old man presents with severe pain radiating from his lower back to the posterior thigh and lateral side of the leg. He reports numbness over the lateral foot and difficulty performing plantar flexion. Physical examination reveals weakness of the hamstring muscles and a decreased Achilles tendon reflex. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A football player experiences severe knee pain and a feeling of instability in his right leg after an injury. Physical examination reveals a positive Lachman test. Which structure is most likely injured?

A 6-year-old girl is brought to the emergency room with a fracture arm. She has blue sclera, bilateral hearing loss, blue-yellow teeth, and a history of multiple fractures in the past few years. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
Which of the following is most likely present 1 month after a bone fracture?

A 15-year-old boy presents with a jaw mass that has been enlarging over the past 5 months. Gross examination reveals a well-demarcated intramedullary lesion with bone expansion but no cortical destruction. Histologic examination shows irregular trabeculae of woven bone within a fibrous stroma. What is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the most common cause of pyogenic osteomyelitis?

A patient presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness and difficulty climbing stairs and raising the arms. The patient also has a Raynaud phenomenon. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient presents with fever, myalgia, periorbital edema, and muscle weakness after eating undercooked pork. A histological section of skeletal muscle is shown below, demonstrating coiled larvae encysted within the muscle fibers. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman presents with bilateral MCP and PIP joint pain and swelling for 6 months. She has morning stiffness lasting 2 hours. Laboratory tests show ACPA positive. X-ray shows joint space narrowing and marginal erosions. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old man presents with chronic knee pain and a mass at the foot for 1 month. Physical examination shows a painful, swollen knee joint and a small mass at his foot. Histology of the mass shows the deposition of pink amorphous materials with foreign body reaction. Which of the following abnormal blood findings is most likely?

A 65-year-old man presents with proximal muscle weakness, dry mouth, a history of smoking, and decreased deep tendon reflexes. Repetitive nerve stimulation shows an incremental response. Which of the following underlying malignancies is most strongly associated with this condition?
Which type of synovial fluid analysis should never involve the use of anticoagulants?

A 54-year-old man presents with sudden, severe pain and swelling of the right big toe. The affected joint is red, warm, and extremely tender. He has a history of chronic kidney disease and drinks alcohol regularly. Joint aspirations are performed. Polarized light microscopy shows needle-shaped crystals with negative birefringence. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman presents with pain and swelling of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints. She reports morning stiffness lasting more than 1 hour. Hand radiographs demonstrate uniform joint space narrowing. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old man presents with a 2-day history of left knee pain without a history of trauma. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 38.3°C. The left knee is painful, swollen, and tender, with a limited range of motion in all directions. A positive ballottement test is also noted. What is the most appropriate initial investigation to establish the diagnosis?

A 70-year-old man presents with fever and right knee pain. Physical examination reveals a red, swollen, and tender right knee with a limited range of motion in all directions. Arthrocentesis reveals cloudy synovial fluid with a WBC count of 95,000 cells/µL (PMN 90%, lymphocytes 10%). No crystals are identified. Gram stain is negative, and the culture result is pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 28-year-old man presents with severe left hip pain after a motorcycle accident. His left hip is flexed, adducted, and internally rotated, and he is unable to move the leg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 45-year-old patient presents with numbness and pain on the plantar surface of the foot. Physical examination shows decreased sensation over the sole of the foot. Which nerve is most likely injured?

A 60-year-old man presents with a mass at the anterolateral aspect of the left leg for 6 months. He has numbness over the upper lateral part of the leg and dorsum of the foot. He has been unable to perform dorsiflexion for 1 month. Which nerve is most likely injured?

A 15-year-old female presents with an abnormal spinal curvature. Physical examination reveals uneven shoulders and waist asymmetry. A standing whole-spine X-ray demonstrates a lateral curvature of the spine with vertebral rotation. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents with low back pain radiating to the lateral aspect of the leg and dorsum of the foot. Physical examination reveals weakness of dorsiflexion of the great toe and decreased sensation over the dorsum of the foot. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
A 62-year-old man presents with severe lower back pain, urinary retention, decreased anal sphincter tone, saddle anesthesia, and asymmetric weakness in both legs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
An elderly woman sustains a distal radius fracture and is treated with a cast. Based on the phase of bone healing, when should the cast usually be removed?
From the picture, which structure is most likely injured?

A 40-year-old man goes out to socialize with friends. After a period of time, he suddenly passes out. Upon waking, he is unable to extend his wrist and has lost sensation over the dorsum of his hand. Which type of peripheral nerve injury is most likely responsible for his symptoms?

choices.D: Mixed peripheral injury of the radial nerve

choices.C: The bony fragments are perfectly stable with absolute stability
choices.D: Relative stability with controlled micromovement and partial weight-bearing

questions.stem: Which of the following enzymes is responsible for the metabolism of succinylcholine, and a deficiency of this enzyme can result in prolonged paralysis after administration of the drug?

A male patient undergoing surgery for prostate cancer receives succinylcholine and halothane during general anesthesia. He subsequently develops severe muscle rigidity, rapidly increasing body temperature, tachycardia, and other signs of a serious adverse reaction. The anesthetic agents are discontinued, and an antidote is administered. What is the mechanism of action of the antidote?

choices.A: Increase calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
choices.C: Inhibit calcium ion (Ca2+) release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
choices.D: Block acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is commonly used as a neuromuscular blocking agent to produce rapid skeletal muscle relaxation during general anesthesia?

A 56-year-old patient with COPD and a history of heavy smoking is scheduled for surgery. A non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent is required for muscle relaxation during anesthesia. Which of the following drugs should be avoided?

An 80-year-old man with a history of ischemic stroke has been taking low-dose aspirin for secondary prevention for several years. He develops lower back pain that persists for 3 weeks. Without consulting a physician, he starts taking ibuprofen several times daily for pain relief. Which of the following adverse drug reactions is most likely in this patient?
